profile.stagger_pattern: Two aldermen per ward on staggered 3-year terms, so one seat in each of Wards I, II and III is up each April, plus the mayor on his or her own 3-year cycle. From 2026 South Dakota requires municipal elections to run with the June primary or November general; Alcester's first such election, 2026-06-02, was cancelled because all petitioners were unopposed, and the terms then issued were re-staggered (Ward I 2-year, Ward III 3-year).

run_log.detail: Read agent-brief.md and the South Dakota registry entry. Registry claims verified: (a) legislativeaudit.sd.gov/reports/City/{City} City {Year}.pdf works - Alcester City 2024.pdf returned HTTP 200, 651KB, with a 'City Officials' page; every other year 2018-2023 and 2025 returned HTTP 404, confirming the registry's 'small towns are audited irregularly'. (b) The directory index legislativeaudit.sd.gov/reports/City/ returns 403. (c) The registry's highest-value SD route - statutory publication of council proceedings by a hyperlocal outlet - was decisive here.

Three wards, two aldermen each (6 seats) plus an elected mayor; 3-year staggered terms; annual April election (2nd Tuesday) through 2025. Confirmed by the 2019-01-07 blog post listing '2019 Election Vacancies: Mayor, Ward I-3 years, Ward II-3 years, Ward III-3 years'. 2026 moved: the 2025-12-01 minutes record a state law change requiring municipal elections to coincide with the June primary or November general; Alcester set 2026-06-02, then cancelled it because the petitioners were unopposed (2026-05-04 minutes).

RUNG 4/5 was the unlock. The hyperlocal blog 'A Voice from the Gallery' (avoicefromthegallery.com), written by a former Alcester council member, reprints each meeting's opening roll call verbatim and covers 2019-01 through 2024-02 densely. It is WordPress.com-hosted: the self-hosted wp-json route 404s, but the public WordPress.com REST API works with no key - public-api.wordpress.com/rest/v1.1/sites/avoicefromthegallery.com/posts/?search=&after=&before=&number=&fields=date,URL,title,content - and ?number=100 with search terms pulled 125 relevant posts in a single call. THIS SHOULD BE ADDED TO THE REGISTRY'S PORTAL-API LIST: every wordpress.com-hosted local outlet is reachable this way. CAUTION: the same blog switched subject city in 2024 - all 2025 posts cover SPIRIT LAKE, IOWA, not Alcester, with a different mayor and council. Reading them as Alcester would have produced a wholly fabricated 2025 roster.

RUNG 6. The census entry for alcester.sdcity.gov/alcester-meeting-agenda-and-minutes is a Wix page whose document list is JS-rendered - no PDF hrefs in the served HTML. The route through it: the served HTML DOES contain the site's page manifest as "pageUriSEO" strings, giving /2024-minutes, /2025-agendas-minutes, /2026-agendas-minutes etc. Those year pages serve real hrefs of the form /_files/ugd/a355fa_{32hex}.pdf to plain curl. 24 (2024) + 22 (2025) + 25 (2026) documents retrieved and extracted with pdftotext -layout; all were text-layer PDFs, so no OCR was needed. The 2020-2023 year pages served ZERO ugd hrefs (different Wix element), but the blog already covered those years. 2019 is genuinely absent from the city site, as the census recorded - the blog covered it instead.

Alcester City 2024 audit report (legislativeaudit.sd.gov) used as an independent cross-check. IT CONTRADICTS THE CITY'S OWN MINUTES: its page is headed 'City Officials / December 31, 2024' and lists Mayor Lisa Hodgson with Hedden, Hatle, Swanson, Tschida, Brian Johnson and Wieseler - but the city's January-April 2025 minutes show Darla Reppe seated and neither Swanson nor Tschida on the council, and both were in fact appointed in May and June 2025. The audit page is therefore a PUBLICATION-DATE roster, not the December 31 snapshot it claims - the 'runs AHEAD of its own fiscal year' failure mode in the cross-state ACFR note, here in a South Dakota legislative audit. Dated primary minutes were preferred throughout.

Alcester is almost entirely mid-term churn: 17 of 30 tenure rows begin by appointment. Dated mid-term changes found: Glas resigns mayor (2020-05-18); Haeder resigns Ward II (2020-04-06), is elected Ward III (2020-04-14), then resigns Ward III and is appointed mayor (2020-05-18); Ireland appointed Ward II (2020-05-18); Vickie Larsen appointed Ward III (2020-07-20) and gone within weeks; Brian Johnson and Curtis Keiser both resign (2021-09-20); Driesen appointed Ward III (2021-10-04); Talbott departs (mid-2022); VandenHul appointed (by 2022-09-19); Driesen elevated to mayor with Hatle and Hedden appointed the same evening (2023-05-01); Sundstrom appointed Ward I (2023-06-20); Peeples departs (autumn 2023); Brian Johnson returns (2023-08-16); Sundstrom resigns (2024-11-07); Hodgson appointed mayor and Wieseler appointed Ward I (2024-12-04); Swanson appointed Ward III (2025-05-05); Tschida appointed Ward I (2025-06-02); Hedden resigns Ward II (2025-12-15); Brian Johnson resigns Ward II (2026-01-13).

All roster text was extracted locally (pdftotext -layout on city PDFs; HTML stripped from the WordPress.com API's raw content field) rather than taken from a page summary. Contradictions resolved and recorded rather than smoothed over: (1) the blog records Cyndi Peeples's 2021-05-03 oath as 'Ward II' while both Ward II seats were filled that same evening by Larsen and Brian Johnson and 2023 contact lists name her Ward I - Ward I adopted; (2) the 2024-05-06 minutes record Darla Reppe's 1-year oath as 'Ward II Alderwoman' while the Ward II lineage is fully accounted for by Hedden and Brian Johnson (each named Ward II in their own resignation records) and her seat was refilled in 2025 as a Ward III vacancy - Ward III adopted; (3) the 2019-05-06 blog post's body dates the meeting 'May 9th, 2019' while its title dates it 05/06 - May 6 2019 was a Monday, the council's normal meeting night, and May 9 a Thursday, so the title is correct. Election dates 2019-04-09, 2020-04-14, 2021-04-13, 2022-04-12, 2023-04-11, 2024-04-09 all check out as second Tuesdays; 2025-04-08 is named explicitly in the 2025-01-07 minutes.

Not needed and not spent: no county or state results portal was queried, per the registry's finding that South Dakota cities administer their own elections and no centralized municipal results exist. sdpublicnotices.com was not needed - the blog and the city's own minutes supplied the proceedings the notices would have carried. The Alcester Union-Hudsonite was never fetched directly; its reporter appears in the blog's meeting accounts.

Wrote raw/2.json. 9 seats tracked (Mayor, Council President, and 6 ward seats as two stable lineages per ward). Seat labels 'Ward N Seat A/B' are this project's construct - Alcester's own records identify seats only by ward, so the A/B split is the tenure lineage, not a city-assigned designation.
